what: Whole generator artifacts that are withdrawn, with the reason. Read by scripts/lib/item-disposition.mjs.
why_this_file_exists: Four dispositions are DERIVED -- inserted (the stem is in the bank), rejected (the standing list or an artifact's reject block), superseded (a later revision names the id), gate-refused (a non-survivor verdict). A fifth cannot be: a probe artifact regenerated by a fuller run leaves no trace anywhere. Its items are not rejected, nothing supersedes them by id, and the gates passed them. Only the person who launched the second run knows the first was a measurement, so that intention is written down once with its reason. Nothing is withdrawn for being OLD -- 'probably superseded by now' is the assumption that produced the task 1.2 over-cap.
read_by: scripts/lib/item-disposition.mjs -- so a withdrawn artifact's survivors do not fill a task's anchor cap
scripts/report-aimsf-completion.mjs -- so they are not counted as awaiting approval

withdrawn.why: A CEILING MEASUREMENT, not a batch. PROMPT-96 s4 ruled the $20 ceiling be measured on the first task, so this run generated task 1.2 alone (4 items, 3 survivors) to derive a per-item cost. AIMSF-R5.json then regenerated 1.2 as part of the full scope, under a different run id and therefore a different anchor draw. Its three survivors were never offered for a read and are not among the 57 the director read.
withdrawn.ruled: PROMPT-97 addendum s1 -- recorded when the census began counting awaiting survivors, because until then a withdrawal had no consequence

not_withdrawn_and_why: AIMSF-R4-PROBE.json and AIMSF-R4-REST.json are BOTH part of round R4. The director read all 29 of their survivors as one set, so neither is a measurement and both carry live verdicts.

AIMSF-S2-INSERT.json and AIMSF-S2-INSERTED.json describe rows that are in the bank; they are excluded by the INSERTED test, which is derived, and must not be listed here -- a withdrawal would hide them from a report that should show them as inserted.

reserved.full_reason: A.10.3 over the cap; a good item, held as a reserve rather than rejected
reserved.why_not_rejected: The item is good. A reject would record it as wrong; it is surplus while its clause is at the cap, which is a fact about the clause and not about the item.
reserved.why_not_awaiting: A reserve that counted in the awaiting layer would fill its clause and refuse an item the director accepted on the same clause. It is queued for when space appears.
